definition: Turi is a graph-based, high performance, distributed computation framework written in C++.
details: The GraphLab project was started by Prof. Carlos Guestrin of Carnegie Mellon University in 2009. It is an open source project that uses the Apache License. While GraphLab was originally developed for machine learning tasks, it has also been developed for other data-mining tasks.

explainer.lead: GraphLab is an open-source C++ framework for running graph-based computations across multiple machines. It matters because large machine-learning and data-mining problems can exceed what one machine can handle comfortably.

tiers.eli5: Imagine a huge puzzle whose pieces are connected by strings, and the puzzle is too big for one person to solve. GraphLab helps a team of computers work on connected pieces of that puzzle at the same time. It was first made for machine learning, but it can help with other kinds of data analysis too.
tiers.practitioner: Use GraphLab when a machine-learning or data-mining task can be expressed as a graph and needs distributed, high-performance computation. It is a C++ framework, so the main design work is representing the problem and its computation in graph form rather than treating it as a single-machine algorithm. Distributed execution also makes deployment and coordination part of the engineering task.
tiers.paperLevel: GraphLab can be described as a graph-based distributed computation framework with high performance as a goal. The project was started by Carlos Guestrin at Carnegie Mellon University in 2009 and is released under the Apache License. Its original focus was machine learning, later extending to other data-mining tasks.

explainer.example: A team analyzing a large social network can represent people as nodes and their connections as edges, then run a machine-learning computation over that graph across multiple machines. The same setup can also support other data-mining analyses of the network.

usedIn.name: Machine learning
usedIn.detail: The original application area for GraphLab's distributed, graph-based computations.

usedIn.name: Data mining
usedIn.detail: GraphLab was also developed for data-mining tasks beyond its initial machine-learning focus.

explainer.intuition: Many computational problems can be represented as connected pieces of data. GraphLab provides a way to express those problems as graphs and distribute the computation across machines.
howItWorks: Express the problem as a graph of connected data.
Associate the required computation with that graph.
Run the computation using GraphLab's C++ framework.
Distribute the work across multiple machines.
Use the results for machine learning or data mining.
explainer.whyItMatters: GraphLab connects graph-based problem representation with distributed computation. That makes it useful for large machine-learning and data-mining tasks where performance and multiple machines matter.
misconceptions: GraphLab is not limited to machine learning; it also supports other data-mining tasks.
It is a distributed computation framework, not a single machine-learning algorithm.
It is an open-source C++ framework under the Apache License, not a hosted service.

diagram.caption: GraphLab turns a graph-based task into distributed computation and returns the analysis results.
